chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyah (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim quoted Al-Yashkari, on the authority of Abu Ahmad Muhammad ibn Zyad al-Azdi, on the authority of Aban ibn Uthman, on the authority of Aban ibn Taqlib, on the authority of Sufyan ibn Abi Layli, on the authority of Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them both)

that he said: In a long narration of his with the Roman Emperor, the Roman Emperor asked him about seven things that God, the Exalted, created which did not come out from a womb, so he said: Adam and Eve, the ram of Abraham, the she-camel of Salih, the snake of Paradise, the raven which God, the Exalted, sent searching in the earth, and Satan, may God, the Blessed and Sublime, curse him.

key_terms.لَمْ تَخْرُمْ مِنْ رَحِمٍ: Did not come out from a womb

ai.seo_question: What are the seven creatures created by God that were not born from a womb according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Khisal*, Imam Al-Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon him) clarifies the theological concept of 'khalaq wa-lan yulad' (created but not born) during a dialogue with the Roman Emperor, distinguishing these seven unique creations from ordinary biological birth. This list highlights key figures and entities in Islamic cosmology, including Adam, Eve, the ram of Abraham, the camel of Salih, the Garden's snake, the raven, and Iblis, emphasizing their direct creation by God without maternal gestation.
